rendered:
When the paper tested discrimination across concentrations, the bacteria that could only be partly told apart were S. typhimurium and S. aureus[1]. Their clusters in the LDA score plots partly overlapped (shown in the supplementary figures). By contrast, P. aeruginosa, E. coli, E. sakazakii, L. monocytogenes, and E. faecium[2] could be fully told apart (Fig. 3[3] shows several of these).

The blind tests were performed on four strains at unknown concentrations, which delivered 100% classification accuracy[4].
